title: Students and community members walk out over flag policy in Sonoma
seoTitle: Sonoma student walkout over pride flags

tea.why: Protesters oppose the school board's new flag policy that forced the removal of the Progress Pride flag from Sonoma Valley High School.
tea.want: Participants want the school board to reverse its new flag policy and keep the pride flag flying.
tea.changed: Oct 13: Hundreds of students and community members gathered outside Sonoma Valley High School to protest the flag policy.

summary: Students and community members in Sonoma, California, staged a walkout and rally outside Sonoma Valley High School to protest a newly approved school board flag policy. The policy, passed by a 3-2 vote on October 8 by the Sonoma Valley Unified School District Board of Trustees, restricts symbolic flags and effectively ended the daily display of the Progress Pride flag that had flown at the high school since 2019. The demonstration was organized by student members of the school's Gender & Sexualities Alliance, alongside local groups Wake UP Sonoma and Sonoma Valley Pride. Protesters chanted, waved rainbow flags, and demanded that the board reconsider its decision and keep the pride flag up. School board President David Bell defended the policy, stating the district must represent all students equally.
demands: Reconsider the new school flag policy
response: School board President David Bell defended the policy, stating that the district's job is to represent all students equally and that no process was originally created for other groups when the flag went up in 2019, according to sources.

updates.text: The Sonoma Valley Unified School District Board of Trustees voted 3-2 to approve a new flag policy restricting symbolic flags.
Hundreds of students and community members participated in a walkout and rally outside Sonoma Valley High School.
